summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease Hb-SS, proteinuria, and a history of hepatitis C presented with a pain crisis involving her back, right leg, chest, and abdomen, likely triggered by dehydration from colonoscopy prep. She was treated with IV fluids and IV narcotics, with transition to oral pain medication as her symptoms improved. A PICC line was placed for reliable access. Chest imaging showed mild pulmonary vascular congestion but no acute chest syndrome or pneumonia. Despite anemia (hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL on discharge), she remained asymptomatic and was not transfused due to prior transfusion-related hepatitis C. Her pain resolved sufficiently for discharge, and she was sent home with an increased dose of hydroxyurea, instructions to follow up with her hematologist, and a plan to check a CBC within the week.
problems: Hb-SS disease with acute chest syndrome
